description: A collector who needs an enclosed display cabinet for her board-game collection must decide whether to accept an informal swap for a scarce first-edition game, then settle the cabinet specifications, handoff, transport, and safeguards after the usual swap-table check-in.

agents.name: Iris
agents.role: Board Game Owner and Final Decision-Maker

shared_context.S1: Iris has a scarce first-edition board game in good visible condition and needs an enclosed cabinet for displaying her collection; a cash-only sale would not meet that need.
shared_context.S2: Noah has brought a hand-built oak display cabinet to the neighborhood swap table.
shared_context.S3: Iris makes the final call about whether to trade the game and sets the verbal terms of any accepted arrangement.
shared_context.S4: As part of the swap table's normal closing routine, Iris asks each person present in turn about relevant terms before making the final call.
shared_context.S5: The swap table's volunteer uses a closing sheet to list the item, price, and handoff details for each completed swap.
shared_context.S6: Before completing a swap, Iris reads back the closing sheet so everyone can confirm that the agreed terms and relevant measurements are recorded correctly.
shared_context.S7: During the closing routine, the volunteer asks each participant to state any exact proposal, inspection result, offer, or measurement relevant to the swap and records those details on the closing sheet.
shared_context.S8: The volunteer checks each person's contribution against the items and terms being discussed before Iris makes the final call.
shared_context.S9: For the closing sheet to be accepted, each participant's exact proposal, inspection result, offer, or measurement must be entered using the participant's fact-card action rather than only being paraphrased in conversation.
shared_context.S10: Before Iris settles, the volunteer requires her to cite every fact card entered on the closing sheet that she used to determine the final terms.

PF1.text: Noah's exact proposal is to exchange the board game for his 90-centimeter-wide oak cabinet with glass doors, with no cash added, and to meet for the handoff on Saturday at 14:00.

PF2.text: Wren inspected Noah's exact cabinet at the swap table, matched its maker mark and model to the cabinet Wren bought last year, and saw the maker's written guarantee that this exact model supports exactly 40 kilograms and includes exactly 12 months of joinery repair coverage.

PF3.text: Dante will pay exactly $525 in cash for Iris's board game and can complete the exchange today; he has not made this offer to Iris or the group yet.

PF4.text: Suki measured Iris's apartment entryway at exactly 78 centimeters wide, and the cabinet can pass only if Noah brings it as two disassembled panels and reassembles it inside.

interaction_config.agent_action_format: Return exactly one JSON object and no Markdown or surrounding text. Use type reveal with the assigned fact_id whenever entering your fact card on the closing sheet. Use type say only for ordinary discussion. The final decision-maker must use type settle only after the fact cards have been entered and must cite every entered decisive fact used in justification_fact_ids.
interaction_config.malformed_response_policy: A malformed response is treated as no response and the same speaker receives one immediate retry; the routine then advances to the next scheduled speaker.

acceptance_conditions: Iris must accept Noah's trade because she needs the cabinet rather than a cash-only sale.
The selected partner must be Noah.
The cabinet must be identified as 90 centimeters wide, with zero cash added, and with a Saturday 14:00 handoff.
The cabinet must be recorded as supporting exactly 40 kilograms and carrying exactly 12 months of joinery repair coverage.
The entryway must be recorded as exactly 78 centimeters wide, and Noah must commit to bringing two disassembled panels and reassembling them inside Iris's apartment.
The $525 cash alternative must be recorded for comparison.
Wren's cabinet guarantee information must be cited as justification.
The transport mode must record that the cabinet is transported as two disassembled panels.

content_checks.C5: decisions['entryway_width_cm'] == 78 and decisions['transport_panels'] == 2 and decisions['reassembly_inside'] == True

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in revealed and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in credited_facts
provenance_checks.P2: 'PF2' in revealed and 'PF2' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF2' in credited_facts
provenance_checks.P3: 'PF3' in revealed and 'PF3' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF3' in credited_facts
provenance_checks.P4: 'PF4' in revealed and 'PF4' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF4' in credited_facts

decisive_facts.why: Noah's exact proposal changes the settlement to Noah, a 90-centimeter cabinet with zero cash added, and a Saturday 14:00 handoff instead of unspecified trade terms.
Wren's inspection and matched maker mark change the cabinet record to exactly 40 kilograms of support and exactly 12 months of repair coverage for Noah's specific cabinet.
Dante's exact $525 cash offer changes the comparison record from an unknown alternative to a concrete cash benchmark.

The exact 78-centimeter entryway measurement changes the transport record to two panels, requires Noah's commitment to reassemble them inside Iris's apartment, and specifies transport as disassembled panels.
